title: Samuel Barber's birth chart
metaDescription: Samuel Barber's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 18.3° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Mercury holds a square to Mars at 0.5° — close enough to weld thinking to drive. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 18.3° into Pisces — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to the Moon. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Mercury holds 26.7° Aquarius, Venus holds 15.5° Aquarius, Mars holds 27.2° Taurus — in the old shorthand, thought that travels by comparison; attraction that begins as conversation; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury to Mars is the closest call of the day, a square within 0.5°. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower. Behind it, the Sun trine Neptune at 1.6°, and Mercury trine Pluto at 1.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Uranus opposes Neptune while both square Saturn. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. Mars in Taurus at 27.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Aries at 21.5° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 air, 2 water, 2 earth, 1 fire by element and 4 cardinal, 3 fixed, 2 mutable by mode. Jupiter and Neptune were retrograde. Pluto changed direction during the day, so its motion is left open.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aquarius into Pisces during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.3° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
